subject: import-normalization
seam_notes: Sidecar `<pdf>.txt` beside the bytes; line 1 is `#parsed-text/1 unpdf@<version> sha256:<16>` — format version, parser identity+version and a source fingerprint, all three required to match. A missing/older/foreign stamp is a loud miss, never a silent pass; an unreadable unpdf version disables the sidecar rather than degrading it to an unverifiable cache (absent-guard-is-loud). Written .part-then-rename; deleteParsedText() is the reaper. Gate green: npm run typecheck clean, unit lane lib/ingest 228/228 (8 new). Second ingest: unpdf invocations 1 -> 0 per PDF, i.e. 23 -> 0 for the slice.
falsifier: Wall time is not the payoff. Measured on this box: 23 parses of a synthetic 55-line posting PDF = 104,7 ms vs 1,6 ms of sidecar reads. The real .justice-samples/ corpus is gitignored and absent from every checkout, so the proposal T1 timing could not be run at all. If the payoff has to be seconds, this is not worth its coherence surface; it is worth it only for the other two forces — re-scoring the corpus when unpdf is absent or bumped, and attributing a diff to the extractor change rather than to a silent re-parse. Divergence from the proposal: it copied LightRAG warn-never-reparse; a version mismatch here re-parses and re-stamps, because warn-never-reparse leaves the corpus permanently mixed (new PDFs still enter at the new engine) while re-parse converges it.

subject: retrieval
seam_notes: Gate: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npm run path-oracle` exit 2 (9 of 9 rows unevaluable) because NO ./.pglite exists on this machine or in the main checkout - the proposal assumed the store is present, and its whole measurable (`rows whose winning path changed across a da:kg-compute --commit`) therefore stays unmeasured here. The instrument itself is proven end-to-end: against a throwaway 4-node/2-edge store seeded with two of the oracle's real documented pairs, --update froze 2 rows, and after mutating that store the check exited 1 naming both clauses correctly - `hop 1 (psp:person:6150 -linked_to-> company:ico:26185610) citation kg-compute/pass-39 -> kg-compute/pass-41-RECOMPUTED` and `pendingCount 1 -> 0 (a tie was reviewed)`. Liveness is asserted before any path is evaluated, so an endpoint that has left the graph is unevaluable, never a silent pass. --update is flag-only, writes only rows that would otherwise fail, never on a green run, and the review surface is the JSON diff. | verdict recorded as unevaluable; instrument that would make it measurable: a local .pglite store (none on this machine) - run `npm run path-oracle -- --update` once against it, then the check pins 9 rows
falsifier: Freeze the 9 rows with `npm run path-oracle -- --update` on the machine that holds ./.pglite, then re-run after the next `da:kg-compute --commit`. If most rows go red on two consecutive refreshes, path ranking is genuinely unstable under data refresh - that is a PRODUCT finding about what the /graf permalink promises a reader, and belongs in docs/routes/graf-permalink.md, not in a looser check. If most rows go `unevaluable` within a term instead, the pairs are keyed on individuals who lose mandates and must be re-keyed on structurally durable entities (party, large organ, long-lived company).

subject: module-design
seam_notes: Measured A/B on the repo's own unit lane, same runner both arms. Arm A: a probe importing readAdminGate and asserting all four verdicts reached 1 of 4 - `not-configured` returns before the cookie read; `locked`, `unauthorized` and `ok` all threw `cookies was called outside a request scope` at accessGate.ts:52. Reachability stopped exactly at the host-bound read. Arm B: cookie jar mirrored to `{expected, submitted}` (two optional strings - only what the verdict reads), all four verdicts moved to a pure decideAdminGate() in lib/security/ (which IS in ALL_TEST_GLOBS; app/** is not), ambient read left in accessGate. 4 of 4 reachable, 6 assertions. Gate green: tsc --noEmit clean, full unit lane 221 files / 3040 tests. Note server-only was NOT the blocker - vitest.shared.ts already aliases it to a stub, which is why lib/security/token.test.ts existed all along; the blocker was next/headers cookies() alone.
falsifier: The shim kept ONE branch on purpose and that is where this could be wrong: readAdminGate still skips the cookie read when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset, because reading cookies opts the route out of static prerendering and a branchless shim would newly make an unconfigured /admin dynamic. If a future Next makes the cookie read free of rendering consequence, the guard is dead weight and the shim should go branchless. Conversely, if anyone adds a second verdict-bearing `return` to accessGate.ts, the extraction has been undone - that, not the branch count, is the check.

Arm A (brief as shipped): 39 of 66 rules ambiguous - the reviewer has no way to tell whether a gradient or tracking observation is its fidelity call or the detector's band check, and every ambiguous finding spends one of 8 capped slots. Arm B (patched): the detector's verdict is inherited as a premise ('treat a condition it did not report as clean on its own rules'), the shared surface is named, and the split is stated as comp-character vs value-in-band, so the ambiguous set is 0 by construction; plus a 5-entry not-reasons list. Behavioural rate not measured - no recorded reviewer returns exist in the tree, and running the agent needs screenshots, an approved comp and a quality card this run did not have. Generated copy hand-patched identically because no local generator exists (the banner's build step ships with the upstream skill); pair re-verified byte-identical after the edit.

subject: mcp-tools
seam: .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/live-wrap.mjs:50 (the --page-url flag), :250 (pageUrl ? [] : pendingEntriesThatMayAffectWrap(...)), :253-259 (the named refusal missing_page_url_with_pending_edits), :261-263 (per-page filter entry.pageUrl !== pageUrl), :458 manualEditMayAffectWrap. The single-seat interactive application is the live browser; the ambient state is which page is open.
what_a_caught_outcome_would_teach: that a fleet tree already resolves the ambient reference correctly, which would validate the corrective by convergence while refuting the claim that it is an unowned gap - and would change what the technique says rather than confirm it.
result: CAUGHT, and it refuted one clause. This tree already implements obligations 1-2 (the browser passes $event.pageUrl explicitly; the tool never reads the current page itself) and implements obligation 3 MORE PRECISELY than the technique stated it. The technique demanded a typed refusal on an absent reference, unconditionally. live-wrap refuses only when the absence could change THIS answer - it computes, from the source range the caller did name, whether any pending edit can reach it (manualEditMayAffectWrap), refuses by name with a hint if so, and proceeds silently if provably not.
change_to_the_corpus: obligation 3 of the newly landed technique was corrected in the same run rather than amended: the refusal is owed exactly when the missing reference could have changed the answer, expressed as a predicate over the real target rather than a policy about the argument. An unconditional refusal would have made the tool unusable on the majority of calls where no ambient state is in play.
change_to_the_project: none, and none is warranted. Applying the technique as originally written would have made this tree worse. Ship 0 is the correct outcome here.
three_cases: wrap call, no pending edits, --page-url omitted: predicate returns 0 entries, the call proceeds. The technique as written would have refused - the common case broken.
wrap call, a pending edit whose originalText falls inside the picked source range, --page-url omitted: refused by name with a hint naming the fix. Both arms refuse; only this one says why.
wrap call with --page-url supplied, a pending edit staged on a different page: entry.pageUrl !== pageUrl skips it, so an edit on /a cannot bleed into /b. That is obligation 2 already working.
return_condition: when a fleet tool surface accepts an ambient reference it reads itself rather than receives - none does today, which is why the technique reached this tree only as a check and not as a change
